sentences.text: 2. The petitioners by invoking the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has challenged the order dated 02.09.2023 passed by the learned J.M.F.C., Chilika in connection with G.R. Case No.306 of 2023 arising out of Balugaon P.S. Case No.109 of 2023, whereby the learned Court below has taken cognizance of the offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/342/294/323/506/34 of I.P.C. against the present petitioners.

3. Initially the F.I.R. was registered against the present accused persons along with the principal accused namely Chandan Bisoi for the alleged commission of offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/294/323/506/34 of I.P.C.

However, after investigation of the case, the police vide its charge sheet No.150 of 2023 dated 21.07.2023 have filed charge-sheet against the principal accused for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n)/342/294/323/506/34 of I.P.C. Since no offence under Section 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. is made out against the present petitioners, the police preferred not to file charge-sheet against these petitioners for the said offences, however, filed charge sheet for the other offences namely 342/294/323/506/34 of I.P.C. The learned Court below vide impugned order dated 02.09.2023 has taken cognizance of all the offences against the petitioners as well as the principal accused namely Chandan Bisoi.

4. Mr. Routray, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that if the trial Court has taken cognizance of the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. against the petitioners despite the fact that the charge-sheet has not filed for the said offence, sufficient reason should have been given for taking cognizance of the such offence.

However, very mechanically, the learned trial Court has taken cognizance of the said offence against the present petitioners without assigning any reasons or discussing any materials form part of the charge-sheet, on the basis of which, the cognizance has Meera @ Mira Pradhan And vs State Of Odisha And Another .... sentences.text: 5. I have perused the charge-sheet and the documents form part of the charge-sheet and also perused the impugned order.

I am of the considered view that Mr. Routray, learned counsel for the petitioners is correct in his submission that if the charge-sheet is not filed for a particular offence by the police and despite that the learned trial Court takes cognizance of certain offences, adequate reasoning should have been given by the learned trial Court justifying the order of cognizance of the offences.
In absence of appropriate reasons given by the learned Court below, the cognizance order is not sustainable.

Hence, I set aside the impugned order dated 02.09.2023 passed by the learned J.M.F.C., Chilika in connection with G.R. Case No.306 of 2023 arising out of Balugaon P.S. Case No.109 of 2023 and remitted back to the learned trial Court to consider the charge-sheet and pass a detailed on cognizance.
6. With this observation, the CRLMC is disposed of.
